rows.vague: Can you make something that cleans up phone numbers? It should be robust.
rows.ready: Write a Python function normalize_phone(s: str) -> str. Target: return only the digits of s, keeping one leading '+' if s starts with '+'. Check: normalize_phone('+1 (415) 555-0100') == '+14155550100' and normalize_phone('020 7946 0958') == '02079460958'. Reply with one ```python block only.

rows.vague: I need a better way to split text into chunks for my app.
rows.ready: Write a Python function chunk(text: str, n: int) -> list[str] that splits text into consecutive pieces of at most n characters, in order, losing nothing. Check: chunk('abcdefg', 3) == ['abc', 'def', 'g'] and chunk('', 3) == []. Reply with one ```python block only.

rows.vague: Write something to work out how long ago a date was, make it nice.
rows.ready: Write a Python function days_between(a: str, b: str) -> int for ISO dates 'YYYY-MM-DD', returning the absolute number of days between them. Check: days_between('2026-10-20', '2026-10-01') == 19 and days_between('2024-02-28', '2024-03-01') == 2. Reply with one ```python block only.

rows.vague: Make a function to validate emails properly.
rows.ready: Write a Python function is_email(s: str) -> bool returning True when s has exactly one '@', a non-empty local part, and a domain with at least one '.' that neither starts nor ends with '.'. Check: is_email('a@b.co') is True, is_email('a@b') is False, is_email('@b.co') is False, is_email('a@@b.co') is False. Reply with one ```python block only.

rows.vague: Could you write a cleaner slug generator for blog posts?
rows.ready: Write a Python function slugify(title: str) -> str: lowercase, every run of characters that are not a-z or 0-9 becomes one '-', no leading or trailing '-'. Check: slugify('Hello, World!') == 'hello-world' and slugify('  Knos  2026 ') == 'knos-2026'. Reply with one ```python block only.

rows.vague: I want to improve how we compute averages, some data is messy.
rows.ready: Write a Python function mean_of_numbers(xs: list) -> float | None that averages only the int and float items of xs (bool excluded) and returns None when there are none. Check: mean_of_numbers([1, 2, 'x', None, 3]) == 2.0 and mean_of_numbers(['a']) is None and mean_of_numbers([True, 4]) == 4.0. Reply with one ```python block only.

rows.vague: Help me deal with duplicates in a list in a smart way.
rows.ready: Write a Python function dedupe(xs: list) -> list that removes repeated items and keeps the first occurrence of each, in the original order. Check: dedupe([3, 1, 3, 2, 1]) == [3, 1, 2] and dedupe([]) == []. Reply with one ```python block only.

rows.vague: Make a quick, modern helper to format money amounts.
rows.ready: Write a Python function fmt_units(micro: int) -> str that formats an amount given in millionths (6 decimals) with exactly 2 decimals and comma thousands separators, rounding half up. Check: fmt_units(1234567890) == '1,234.57' and fmt_units(5) == '0.00' and fmt_units(1_005_000) == '1.01'. Reply with one ```python block only.

rows.vague: Write a function that checks whether brackets in code are fine.
rows.ready: Write a Python function balanced(s: str) -> bool returning True when every (, [ and { in s is closed by the matching bracket in the right order; other characters are ignored. Check: balanced('f(a[1]{x})') is True, balanced('(]') is False, balanced('((') is False, balanced('') is True. Reply with one ```python block only.

rows.vague: Can you make the word counter better?
rows.ready: Write a Python function top_words(text: str, k: int) -> list[tuple[str, int]] returning the k most frequent lowercase words (a word is a run of letters a-z), most frequent first, ties broken alphabetically. Check: top_words('b a b c a b', 2) == [('b', 3), ('a', 2)] and top_words('', 3) == []. Reply with one ```python block only.
